analyst_observations: The skill's main advantage is in spec-creation: it produced correct test.step() structure and import paths, while the baseline used comment-based steps and a wrong deep relative import path.
For fixture-reference, both produced identical quality — the baseline explored the codebase thoroughly enough to match the skill's output. This assertion set is non-discriminating for this eval.
For selector-lookup, both scored perfectly — the baseline agent grepped data-testid from source and produced equally comprehensive results. This assertion set is also non-discriminating.
The skill saved ~22s on average per run (72.3s vs 94.2s) and used ~10% fewer tokens (34.5k vs 38.3k), likely because it didn't need to explore the codebase for conventions.
The biggest qualitative win: the with-skill spec is directly usable as a real spec file (correct imports, correct structure). The without-skill spec would need manual fixes before it could run.
